subject: Renewal restructure: multi-year ramp + migration trigger & burn-shelf
messages:
From: Samir Shah <samir.shah@avadata.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: contracts@avadata.com
Date: Fri, 28 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal timing + planned migration burst in Q4

Jonas —

We're starting to pull together our renewal planning for Oct 1. Usage has grown faster than we forecasted (mostly embeddings + reranking). We're looking at a multi-year commitment but need two things to align: (1) a smooth ramp (we'd like front-loaded burst capacity for a migration window in Nov) and (2) co-terming the various product SKUs so finance can forecast.

Can you share options for a 24–36 month structure that includes a predictable burst window and safety credits (burn-shelf) while keeping unit pricing friendly? Procurement has been CC'd — they prefer a single contract and co-term if possible.

Thanks,
Samir
Director of Data Platforms, Ava Data

Attachments: none
From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: Samir Shah <samir.shah@avadata.com>
Cc: contracts@avadata.com
Date: Mon, 31 Jul 2028 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal timing + planned migration burst in Q4

Samir — thanks for the heads up and congrats on the growth. High level proposal attached. Key points: 

- Structure: 3-year term with annual true-up windows or a 2-year with an optional 12-month extension (we laid both out in the doc).
- Ramp: front-loaded burst (one-time migration credit equal to 3x your average monthly usage) available in the first 90 days of year 2 to cover the Nov migration spike.
- Co-terming: we'll consolidate embeddings/serve/rerank SKUs under a single Master SOW and co-term to Oct 1.
- Burn-shelf: separate pool of committed credits that auto-deploy for overages during the burst window; unused credits roll forward for one quarter.

I've attached RW-terms-proposal-v1.pdf and the mutual action plan (mep-mutual-action-plan.docx) for procurement. If that lines up, next step is a short internal review and then I can circulate a pricing worksheet + DocuSign.

Proposed next steps: quick sync (30m) this week to confirm ramp numbers, then we route to procurement/legal. Available windows: Wed 8/2 10a–12p PT or Thu 8/3 1p–4p PT.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0132

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 02 Aug 2028 08:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Ava Data renewal — pricing guidance

Jonas / Marissa — looped in for pricing and approvals. I reviewed Samir's usage trend and Jonas' proposed structure. Quick guidance:

- Approve 3-yr plan at up to 22% list discount with the migration credit baked into year 2.
- If they opt for 2-yr + 1yr extension, we hold 18% discount and a smaller migration credit (2x avg month).
- Need legal to confirm that the burn-shelf rollover is limited to one quarter (no multi-year accumulation).

Marissa — please prepare a single-line pricing worksheet (pricing-table-avadata-3yr.xlsx) we can send to Samir once the MAP is agreed. Also confirm any SLO credit language we should include for the burst window.

Thanks — Karthik
VP, Sales

Samir — following up with a consolidated plan. Per our internal review we can do: 

1) 36-month co-term Master SOW, co-terminating 10/1. Yearly true-ups.
2) Migration credit: 3x monthly avg (applied as token credit in Year 2, valid for first 90 days of Y2 — covers Nov migration).
3) Burn-shelf: separate credit pool, unused balance rolls forward one quarter only; no indefinite accumulation.
4) Pricing: 22% discount on list for 3-year commit. If you prefer 24 months + optional 12-month extension, discount is 18%.

Next steps: confirm the preferred term (36mo vs 24+opt1) and estimated migration uplift (what is the expected peak tokens/sec or % uplift vs avg?). Once you confirm, I'll push the pricing worksheet and DocuSign link.

Proposed quick sync: Thu 8/10 9:30a PT or Fri 8/11 11:00a PT — which works?

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
